title: Toyota Tacoma Structure complaint cluster
summary: 64 complaints cluster around door, handle, door handle, open, driver, inside. Status: EMERGING.

claims.text: Owners of 2015-2026 TOYOTA TACOMA describe a recurring structure problem (door, handle, door handle, open, driver, inside).

C-11740765.text: The interior driver side door handle on my 2025 Toyota Tacoma failed and wouldn't open the door from the inside.  I had to roll down my window to open from the outside.  The dealership replaced the handle assembly under warranty.  This happened at around 9300 miles on the odometer.

C-11770160.text: The driver door handle internal mechanism broke under normal operation, preventing exit from the vehicle.  This is a serious safety issue because the driver is literally trapped in the vehicle, unless they roll the window down and engage the handle from the outside, or crawl over the center console to the passenger door.  This is a potentially life-threatening issue.  This problem has been identified, confirmed, and documented by my local official Toyota dealership.  Neither the police nor my insurance company have inspected the door.  No warning lamps, messages, or other symptoms of the probl...

C-11752124.text: The drivers door handle inside the truck has failed leaving me unable to open the drivers door unless I roll the window down and open the door from the outside. I took the truck to a local dealer and they let me know this is a very common problem on the truck and the parts to fix it are on nationwide back order. Was sent home with the vehicle knowing the door is inoperable unless opened from the outside. This poses a serious safety risk in the event of an accident or emergency where one needs to exit the vehicle quickly.

R-22V422000.text: The exterior driver-side door handle may not be assembled properly, which can prevent the opening of the driver-side door from the outside.
R-22V422000.consequence: A person may become trapped which, in the event of an emergency, may increase their risk of injury.

R-24V485000.text: The rear emergency door exterior handle may unexpectedly break under applied force.
R-24V485000.consequence: In the event of an emergency, a broken door handle can prevent or delay emergency responders from entering the vehicle, increasing the risk of injury.

R-20V151000.text: The interior door handle mechanism may fail, resulting in the vehicle's door being unable to be opened by using the inside door handle.
R-20V151000.consequence: If a door cannot be opened with the interior handle in the case of an emergency, it can increase the risk of injury for the driver or passenger.

R-24V484000.text: The rear emergency door exterior handle may unexpectedly break under applied force.
R-24V484000.consequence: In the event of an emergency, a broken door handle can prevent or delay emergency responders from entering the bus, increasing the risk of injury.

R-14V239000.text: Due to an assembly misalignment between the exterior door handle and the door outer panel, the affected vehicles have doors that may be difficult to close or may possibly open while driving.
R-14V239000.consequence: A door that opens unexpectedly may result in an unrestrained occupant falling from the vehicle, increasing the risk of injury.

R-23V480000.text: An electrical connection inside the steering column's spiral cable assembly may be insufficiently welded, causing the connection to separate and deactivate the driver's air bag.  As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard number 208, "Occupant Crash Protection."

R-25V040000.text: An electrical connection inside the steering column's spiral cable assembly may be insufficiently welded, causing the connection to separate and deactivate the driver's air bag. R-22V520000.text: One or more of the individual welds in the upper child seat anchors may be insufficient.  As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard number 225, "Child Restraint Anchorage System."
